key_insight: Lattice Boltzmann can be viewed as a physics-programmed information-processing machine whose relaxation-and-shift updates generate closed macroscopic transport laws.
engineering_relevance: This perspective offers a framework for assessing whether new physics-based or learned components preserve the structure needed for macroscopic transport behavior.
method: Frame lattice Boltzmann updates as iterated relaxation dynamics related to residual networks and transformers.
Identify three update properties sufficient for closed macroscopic laws to emerge.
Test the framework with random targets on a lattice and a traffic-trained network on a graph.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that random targets generate transport laws predicted by their moments and that a traffic-trained graph network generates its own conservation law, without providing quantitative metrics.
watch_item: The mechanism fails when non-conserved modes cease to be damped, and the lattice-level macroscopic law may not warn of this failure.
